expectations.text: Uses the `spacing` prop (not `gap`) on the Flex container, because the bound variable's path contains the segment "spacing"
expectations.evidence: Baseline doesn't use Hearth React at all (no Flex/spacing prop) — it hand-writes CSS: `gap: var(--spacing-lg);` inside a `<style>` block. Uses `gap`, and it isn't even a component-library prop.

expectations.text: Uses the tier name `lg` for the spacing prop, not a raw pixel value like 24 or 16
expectations.evidence: `--spacing-lg: 24px;` overridden to `16px` under a media query — both raw pixel values are hardcoded, not a single named tier.

expectations.text: Does not treat the two different resolved pixel values (24px, 16px) as a reason to pick one over the other — matches by variable name only
expectations.evidence: notes.md/JSDoc: 'modelled here as a CSS custom property with a media-query override, rather than two separate hardcoded numbers' — this is exactly the anti-pattern the rule warns against: treating the two resolved pixel values as two responsive states to encode, instead of one named tier.

expectations.text: Does not render the "Muted subtitle" text node unconditionally in the default view, since it is flagged hidden: true
expectations.evidence: The subtitle is not present anywhere in PromoBanner.tsx.

expectations.text: If the hidden node is rendered at all, does so only with an explicit comment/flag and a question back to the user, not silently
expectations.evidence: Vacuously true — not rendered. Baseline's notes.md does flag the omission explicitly as a deliberate choice.

workarounds: Used a placeholder inline SVG in place of StarMediumIcon since no icon library was specified

eval_feedback.overall: Strong discriminating eval — baseline fails exactly the three assertions that require the figma-implementation mechanical rule, and passes only the two that are satisfiable by generic caution.
